**This census reads signatures.** For the plane family a signature census is
not enough to scope against (F103, and F104 which measures it), so the
companion `phase9_plane_census.md` — `rust/tools/phase9_plane_callers.py` —
reads the **call sites** instead and classifies each operand by the surface it
names (source / reference / reconstruction / SMbCache / coefficient). Read both.

## 1. The correction this census makes

The charter (`prompts/phase9.md` §2) reports **419 body-only** sites that
"fall out as their callees go safe — not converted directly". That number is an
artefact of reading only the **first line** of each tagged item: the port wraps
signatures past 100 columns, so a multi-line signature's first line is bare
(`pub unsafe fn WelsDctMb(`) and the site was filed as having no raw parameter.

Measured at the charter's own commit `aabd0da5` (695 tags), reading the whole
parameter list gives **147** body-only, not 419 — **272 sites** carry raw
parameters and need a signature conversion in some family's session. That is
F101, and it is the number the phase estimate rests on. For comparison, forcing
this tool to look at the first line only reproduces the charter's table almost
exactly: 420/121/51/36/39/19/9 against its 419/120/51/33/31/25/15.

At **this** commit the body-only set is **177** of **303** `port-raw(Phase 9)` tags; the two figures differ as conversions land.

## 2. Families, in dependency order

`pure` = every raw parameter is of this family, so this family's session can
convert the site unaided. `blocked` = the site's *latest* family is this one but
it also carries earlier families, so it converts here only after those land.
`pure + blocked` is the family's real workload.

**`pure` is a property of the signature, not of the call sites.** A kernel can
have a single-family signature and still be unconvertible, because what its
callers *pass* comes from elsewhere. The coefficient family is the worked
example (F103): at `aabd0da5` 19 sites were coeff-pure, but only 5 had a direct
caller passing an owned `[i16; N]` — those 5 converted in T9.A3/A4 and are gone
from the table above. The other 14 sit in `SWelsFuncPtrList` slots with no direct
caller outside their own unit tests, and the 59 call-through sites pass
**SMbCache-derived walking cursors** (`pRes = md::coeff_level(pMbCache)`, then
`pRes.add(64)` per quadrant). Those slots wait on family 3, not family 5.
Sessions B-E should expect the same gap and read their call sites before
scoping — `--family <name>` lists the signatures, but only a grep of the callers
says what is actually reachable.

| # | family   | what it is                            | pure | blocked | total |
|---|----------|---------------------------------------|------|---------|-------|
| 1 | coeff    | Coefficient buffers                   | 0    | 0       | 0     |
| 2 | plane    | Plane / byte cursors                  | 17   | 3       | 20    |
| 3 | mbcache  | MB metadata                           | 0    | 1       | 1     |
| 4 | layer    | Layer / picture / slice               | 13   | 0       | 13    |
| 5 | dispatch | Dispatch tables                       | 1    | 0       | 1     |
| 6 | other    | Other raw signatures                  | 71   | 15      | 86    |
| 7 | ctx      | Context parameter                     | 2    | 3       | 5     |
| — | body     | Body-only                             | 177  | 0       | 177   |
| — | stmt     | Statement-level allows (no signature) | 0    | 0       | 0     |

Total `port-raw(Phase 9)`: **303**.

- **coeff** — `*mut i16` / `*const i16` DCT, Hadamard, quant, scan and NZC blocks. Kernels are already safe; the `unsafe` is a shim wrapping each for a raw caller.
- **plane** — `*mut u8` plane and prediction cursors, and with them `common/`'s mc / sad / deblocking / intra-pred shims.
- **mbcache** — `*mut SMbCache` / `*mut SMB` per-macroblock metadata — the encoder's `MbGrid` analogue.
- **layer** — `*mut SDqLayer` / `SSlice` / `SPicture` and the slice-argument and slicing-stack pointers reached as owned storage.
- **dispatch** — `SWelsFuncPtrList` slots and the fn-pointer types — de-virtualized the way Phase 4a did `pfMdCost`.
- **other** — Bitstream writers, parameter sets, the rate controller, LTR, VAA and scalar out-parameters. Not one family; see the sub-group table.
- **ctx** — `*mut sWelsEncCtx`. **Blocked** until every cursor above retires (F66).
- **body** — No raw pointer in the signature; unsafe only because the body derefs a cursor or calls an unsafe fn. Not converted directly — goes safe when its callees do.

## 4. What each family waits on

```
  coeff ---+
  plane ---+
  mbcache -+--> ctx (F66: a &mut ctx retag invalidates all 65 fields,
  layer ---+          so every context-derived cursor must retire first)
             |
  dispatch --+ (independent of the cursor spine; can run any time)
             |
             v
           body (147 sites: no signature change, they go safe when callees do)
```

`other` is not one family — it is bitstream, parameter-set, rate-control, LTR,
VAA, deblock, trace and scalar out-parameters, each independent of the others
and of the cursor spine except where it also carries a context parameter.

| `other` sub-group | type occurrences |
|-------------------|------------------|
| scalar            | 57               |
| paramset          | 35               |
| bitstream         | 19               |
| trace             | 17               |
| ltr               | 7                |
| vaa               | 4                |
| rc                | 1                |

## 6. Scoping the remaining sessions

Sizes are `pure` (convertible by that session alone) and `total` (its full
workload once the earlier families have landed). The charter's §8 table is
scoped off the first-line numbers and is superseded by this one.

| family   | session | pure | total | note                                                                                                                                                                   |
|----------|---------|------|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| coeff    | A -> D  | 0    | 0     | session A converted the 5 with a direct caller; the 14 left are table slots that follow their data into family 3 (F103)                                                |
| plane    | B-C     | 17   | 20    | largest cursor family; pulls `common/`'s mc/sad/intra-pred shims with it                                                                                               |
| mbcache  | D       | 0    | 1     | 45 pure — 3x the charter's 15 — **plus the 14 coefficient slot types and their 59 call-throughs**; `svc_mode_decision.rs` 19, `svc_set_mb_syn_cabac.rs` 11, `md.rs` 11 |
| layer    | E       | 13   | 13    | 47 pure — `svc_encode_slice.rs` 21, `svc_enc_slice_segment.rs` 11                                                                                                      |
| dispatch | F       | 1    | 1     | the 5 signature sites plus the 22 `cursor` survivors                                                                                                                   |
| other    | ?       | 71   | 86    | **unscoped in the charter** — 123 sites, 7 unrelated sub-groups; needs its own split                                                                                   |
| ctx      | G-H     | 2    | 5     | F66's conversion; 111 pure is the set `q1c.py` gates                                                                                                                   |
| body     | -       | —    | 177   | no conversion; audited at the phase close once the callees are safe                                                                                                    |

Two things the charter does not budget for:

1. **`other` is 123 sites and has no owner.** It is not one family — bitstream,
   parameter sets, RC, LTR, VAA, deblock, trace and scalar out-parameters. 80 of
   them are pure and independent of the cursor spine, so they can run in parallel
   with B-E, but somebody has to be given them.
2. **`ctx` is 234, not 120.** 111 are ctx-only (F66's 109 convertible plus the two
   `*mut *mut sWelsEncCtx` out-parameters); the other 123 carry a cursor *as well*
   as the context, so they convert only after that cursor's family lands. The
   ctx session is therefore last in fact as well as in principle.
